newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bonds sold at close as more profit-taking seen.
newsitem.headline: NZ bonds sold at close as more profit-taking seen.

* NZ yields rise in anticipation of more profit-taking
* Cooling NZ dollar takes downward pressure off rates
* Mkt cautious but could rally when profit-taking subsides
New Zealand debt securities were sold into the close on Wednesday as traders, cautious of continued profit-taking by offshore investors, tried to take short positions.
"Traders tonight really don't want to go home long or square, they want to go home short and there's a little bit of selling creeping in now," a dealer said.
"These guys are expecting to be given some bonds tonight."

Yields opened around 10 basis points across the curve as offshore investors took profit from the recent rally which saw the 90-day bill rate fall to 9.25 percent and the long bond yield fall to 7.26 percent.

Dealers said the recent surge in the New Zealand dollar up to around 71.5 US cents had triggered the debt market rally, and now that the currency was cooling off, the downward pressure of rates was subsiding.
There had been a continuation of Asian and Japanese buying during the session, which had helped to anchor yields, but not enough to compensate for the rash of selling this morning.
The 90-day bill rate ended 11 points higher at 9.37 percent but bonds fared worse, the 11/06 yield rising 17 points to 7.45 percent.
"I don't believe it's the political situation," the dealer said in reference to on-going coalition talks between the main political parties to form a new government.
"It's the potential profit-taking by the offshore investor which is just giving the market a little cause for concern at the moment."
He said if more offshore selling failed to eventuate, the 11/06 bond yield could fall back below 7.40 percent.
"If there's no more offshore selling, we could quite easily see the market rally, not to where it was, but at least down through 7.40 (percent) again," he said.
